facts.statement: The genus Megapiranha was described by Cione and colleagues in 2009.
Megapiranha lived in Argentina during the Late Miocene, approximately 8 to 10 million years ago.
facts.quote: Late Miocene (8–10 million years ago) Ituzaingó Formation of Argentina

facts.statement: Based on later research, Megapiranha is estimated to have reached a length of 71 cm and a weight of 10 kg.
facts.quote: It is thought to have been about 71 cm in length and 10 kg in weight

facts.statement: The estimated bite force of Megapiranha ranges from 1,240 to 4,749 Newtons.
facts.quote: Its bite force is estimated between 1,240 – 4,749 N

facts.statement: The holotype fragment was rediscovered by Alberto Luis Cione in the collection of the Museo de La Plata.
facts.quote: The specimen, a fragment of the animal's premaxilla containing several teeth, was later rediscovered by Alberto Luis Cione in the collection of the Museo de La Plata

facts.statement: The preserved premaxilla of Megapiranha is 6.9 cm long and features a rugose outer surface likely housing nerves and blood vessels.
facts.quote: The entire premaxilla is 6.9 cm long with a rugose outer surface that most likely housed nerves and blood vessels

facts.statement: In Megapiranha, the first and third teeth formed the inner row while the remaining teeth formed the outer row.
facts.quote: Of these teeth the first and third formed the inner row, while the rest formed the outer row

facts.statement: The teeth of Megapiranha feature a single crown shaped like an almost equilateral triangle.
facts.quote: Each teeth only shows a single tooth crown the shape of an almost equilateral triangle

facts.statement: Megapiranha combines traits from basal serrasalmids with those of derived members, representing an intermediate form.
facts.quote: Megapiranha combines several traits known from more basal serrasalmids with those of derived members

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Megapiranha's dentition may not have been solely for carnivory but allowed it to consume a wide range of food sources.
facts.quote: Cione and colleagues suggest that the dentition of Megapiranha may not have been a direct adaptation towards carnivory and likely helped the animal with a wide range of food sources

facts.statement: Tests on a replica suggest Megapiranha could penetrate bovine femurs, turtle shells, and catfish armor.
facts.quote: Tests using a bronze-alloy replica of Megapiranha's dentition showed that it would be able to penetrate the thick outer layer of a bovine femur, the shell of a turtle and the armor of certain catfish species

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Megapiranha fed on hard-shelled animals and larger mammals remains hypothetical due to a lack of fossil evidence like bite marks.
facts.quote: this ecology is only hypothetical in the absence of any fossil material bearing the bite marks of Megapiranha

facts.statement: Megapiranha is classified as a transitional fossil within the subfamily Serrasalminae.
facts.quote: †Megapiranha Category:Serrasalminae Category:Prehistoric ray-finned fish genera Category:Transitional fossils Category:Miocene fish Category:Miocene animals of South America Category:Neogene Argentina Category:Fossils of Argentina Category:Ituzaingó Formation Category:Paraná Basin Category:Fossil taxa described in 2009 Category:Tooth taxa

facts.statement: The time range for Megapiranha is recorded as the Tortonian to Zanclean stages, from 8 to 5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Zanclean (8 to 5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Megapiranha belongs to the family Serrasalmidae.
